messages:
Taylor: hi everyone, first week here. running `docker-compose up` for local dev but Postgres keeps dying during init with "PG_VERSION mismatch" and my app errors with "relation "users" does not exist". i'm on an M1 mac. any quick tips?
Nia: welcome! that PG_VERSION message usually means an existing data dir from a different major PG version. are you bind-mounting a host folder into `/var/lib/postgresql/data`?
Taylor: yup my compose has `- ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` because i wanted to persist data between restarts.
Omar: on mac that often causes permission and architecture mismatches. we recommend using a named volume instead so Docker manages it. change to `- pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` and add `volumes:
  pgdata:` at the bottom. then `docker-compose down -v` and `docker-compose up`.
DevEx: also run `./dev/setup-db.sh` after the DB is ready; it runs migrations/seeds. we add a healthcheck in compose so scripts wait for readiness.
Taylor: switched to named volume and restarted — logs show "database system is ready to accept connections". ran setup script and tests pass. thanks!
Taylor: one more quick question: my app on host couldn't reach redis container at localhost:6379 earlier. any gotchas?
Nia: if your app runs on the host, port mapping should work. sometimes Docker Desktop's port forwarding or the new virtualization framework causes flakiness on mac. a reliable workaround is to run the web app in a container or use `host.docker.internal` from containers to talk to host.
infra-bot: FYI: onboarding checklist includes a short note about named volumes for Postgres on mac and `dev/setup-db.sh`.
Taylor: perfect, will add a note to my onboarding task list. thanks again :tada:
